description: Binning contract shared by the Python atlas pipeline and the web explorer. Change binning only by creating a new version.

D_msh.definition: geometric depth (|r_norm| - R_mp,ref(theta)) / (R_bs,ref(theta) - R_mp,ref(theta)) of the normalized position between the reference boundaries; values inside the clip band but outside the edges go to the first/last bin, others are dropped. It differs from the served R_norm by |dD| < 0.09 for 95 % of samples.

theta_deg.definition: arccos(X/|r|) of the boundary-normalized position (X/Y/Z_gsm_norm); 0 = subsolar

phi_deg.definition: atan2(Z, Y) of the normalized position in the chosen frame, wrapped to [0, 360); 90 = +Z

frames.PGSM: rotation about X_GSM by the sample's own IMF clock angle, so that the IMF component perpendicular to X points to +Z
frames.PGSM_fold: PGSM, then for samples with Bx_imf < 0: magnetic vectors B -> -B and a 180 deg rotation about X, so the quasi-parallel side is always +Z

clock_deg.definition: atan2(By_imf, Bz_imf) wrapped to [0, 360); 0 = northward IMF, 90 = +By

histogram.quantile_method: cumulative counts, linear interpolation inside the bin in the axis scale (log10 for log axes)

neff.definition: number of distinct (spacecraft, hour) intervals; an optional overlay that hatches cells dominated by few spacecraft passes

row_filter: SW_pairing and Norma_pos are true, and the IMF and normalized position are finite

knn.definition: k is counted in neighbours of the full dataset (default 7000, as in the MANGO statistical studies). Tools holding a random fraction f of the samples search round(k*f) neighbours, which covers the same neighbourhood. Neighbours are the nearest samples (Euclidean, R_E) among the normalized positions rotated into the chosen frame; NaN when the distance of the ceil(k/2)-th nearest exceeds cap_re. Only neighbours within search_factor*cap_re are searched. Quantiles use linear interpolation of the neighbours' values in axis space. The sample table keeps a deterministic random fraction (sample_fraction) of the samples; time plays no role.

reference_boundaries.definition: x = nose - rho^2/(4 p) about +X (R_E). MANGO normalizes magnetosheath positions (X/Y/Z_gsm_norm) radially between two fixed reference surfaces; these paraboloids are fitted to the served positions (scripts/fit_reference_boundaries.py, dataset 2026.0: median |residual| 0.12 R_E). The exact surfaces are not published with the data.

voxels.definition: Per (frame, condition bin, voxel) the number of samples and the sum of the raw value of each quantity (finite values only). Voxels are cubes of size_re in the normalized frame coordinates; id = (i<<20)|(j<<10)|k with i = floor(x/size_re)+index_offset (same for j with y, k with z).
voxels.knn: For a node, voxels are ordered by the distance d from the node to their centre (ties by id); their counts are accumulated until k samples are reached (the last voxel contributes only the samples still needed). NaN when fewer than ceil(k/2) samples lie within search_factor*cap_re, or when the voxel where the cumulative count reaches ceil(k/2) is farther than cap_re. Value = sum_v w_v * f_v * S_v / sum_v w_v * f_v * N_v with f_v the used fraction of voxel v, S_v and N_v its sum and count, and w_v = 1/max(d_v, size_re/2) for the distance-weighted mean (sklearn KNeighborsRegressor weights='distance') or 1 for the plain mean.

vectors.mapping: Each sample's GSM vector is pushed forward through MANGO's radial normalization r_n = R*_mp + D (R*_bs - R*_mp), D = (r - R_mp)/(R_bs - R_mp): v_r,n = (dR*/dR) v_r + [R*_mp' + D dR*' - dR* (R_mp' + D dR')/dR] v_theta / r, v_theta,n = (r_n/r) v_theta, v_phi,n = (r_n/r) v_phi, with ' = d/dtheta, dR = R_bs - R_mp, * = reference_boundaries. The sample's slopes are the reference slopes scaled by R_mp/R*_mp and R_bs/R*_bs (approximation A1).
vectors.frame: Rotated about X like positions; magnetic vectors flip sign under PGSM_fold when Bx_imf < 0.
vectors.voxels: Voxel quantities <name>_x, <name>_y, <name>_z: per (frame, condition bin, voxel) the count of samples with all three mapped components finite and the sum of each component in the frame. The vector field is the voxel k-NN mean of each component (voxels.knn, distance-weighted).
